This is the Excalidraw monorepo (c:\excalidraw). I'm implementing a feature: when a user saves/opens a local file in the Excalidraw web app, the browser tab title and/or URL should reflect the file's name.

I need you to research (read-only, no edits) and report back with specifics:

1. In `excalidraw-app/` folder, find where files are saved to disk (e.g. "Save to disk" / "Save As" functionality) and where files are opened/loaded from disk. Look for functions like `saveAsJSON`, `loadFromJSON`, `fileOpen`, `fileSave` etc. Report exact file paths and line numbers, and the relevant function signatures.

2. Find where the document title (`document.title`) is currently set, if anywhere, in `excalidraw-app/` or `packages/excalidraw/`. Also check if there's any existing "app name" or title-setting logic.

3. Find how the app currently manages the URL (e.g. using `history.pushState`, React Router, or similar) in `excalidraw-app/`. Report exact files/functions used to read/write query params or path segments (e.g. for scene id, collaboration room, etc.)

4. Look at `packages/excalidraw/data/filesystem.ts` or similar for `fileOpen`/`fileSave` wrapper utilities, and report their type signatures - specifically whether the returned/opened File object exposes a `.name` property, and whether the save function accepts/returns a file name.

5. Check if there's any existing state (e.g. in AppState or a React context) that stores the currently loaded file's name.

6. Check `excalidraw-app/index.tsx` and `excalidraw-app/App.tsx` (or wherever the app root is) for how local storage / scene loading happens on startup, since we'll want to know if a file name should persist across reloads.

Report back concisely with file paths, line numbers, and short code excerpts for each of the 6 items. Do not make any edits.

```text
268	const _clearAppStateForStorage = <
269	  ExportType extends "export" | "browser" | "server",
270	>(
271	  appState: Partial<AppState>,
272	  exportType: ExportType,
273	) => {
274	  type ExportableKeys = {
275	    [K in keyof typeof APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF]: typeof APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF[K][ExportType] extends true
276	      ? K
277	      : never;
278	  }[keyof typeof APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF];
279	  const stateForExport = {} as { [K in ExportableKeys]?: typeof appState[K] };
280	  for (const key of Object.keys(appState) as (keyof typeof appState)[]) {
281	    const propConfig = APP_STATE_STORAGE_CONF[key];
282	    if (propConfig?.[exportType]) {
283	      const nextValue = appState[key];
284	
285	      // https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/31445
286	      (stateForExport as any)[key] = nextValue;
287	    }
288	  }
289	  return stateForExport;
290	};
```

    - Because `loadFromJSON`/`actionLoadScene` don't currently propagate the opened `File.name` into `appState.name` (see #1/#5), a locally-opened file's on-disk name is not tracked separately from the (optional, manually-set) `appState.name` project title.
  
  ## Key takeaways for implementing the feature
  1. `appState.name` is the natural field to drive the tab title/URL — it already exists, has a rename UI, and persists in localStorage across reloads.
  2. To reflect the actual opened file's name, `loadFromJSON` (`packages/excalidraw/data/json.ts:102`) would need to be changed to also capture `file.name` (stripped of extension) and feed it into the returned `appState.name`, since `loadSceneOrLibraryFromBlob` currently only takes `name` from the JSON content's own `appState.name` (often absent, since export strips it — see #5).
  2b. Optionally also change `appState.ts:217` so `name` has `export: true`, so a file saved from the app round-trips its display name inside the `.excalidraw` file itself.
  3. `document.title` is set nowhere presently — new code (likely a `useEffect` in `excalidraw-app/App.tsx` watching `appState.name`, or watching `excalidrawAPI.getAppState().name`) would be the cleanest hook point.
  4. URL reflection would be new territory — the closest existing pattern is `window.history.replaceState({}, title, url)` used in `App.tsx` (lines 283/300/303) and `Collab.tsx` (line 384), so setting a query/hash param for the file name could follow that same convention, but there is no current path/query mechanism carrying a "file name"; it would need to be added (e.g. `?title=` or similar), being careful not to collide with `id`, `json`, `url`, or `room` hash/query handling in `initializeScene`.

```text
11	type FILE_EXTENSION = Exclude<keyof typeof MIME_TYPES, "binary">;
12	
13	export const fileOpen = async <M extends boolean | undefined = false>(opts: {
14	  extensions?: FILE_EXTENSION[];
15	  description: string;
16	  multiple?: M;
17	}): Promise<M extends false | undefined ? File : File[]> => {
18	  // an unsafe TS hack, alas not much we can do AFAIK
19	  type RetType = M extends false | undefined ? File : File[];
20	
21	  const mimeTypes = opts.extensions?.reduce((mimeTypes, type) => {
22	    mimeTypes.push(MIME_TYPES[type]);
23	
24	    return mimeTypes;
25	  }, [] as string[]);
26	
27	  const extensions = opts.extensions?.reduce((acc, ext) => {
28	    if (ext === "jpg") {
29	      return acc.concat(".jpg", ".jpeg");
30	    }
31	    return acc.concat(`.${ext}`);
32	  }, [] as string[]);
33	
34	  const files = await _fileOpen({
35	    description: opts.description,
36	    extensions,
37	    mimeTypes,
38	    multiple: opts.multiple ?? false,
39	  });
40	
41	  if (Array.isArray(files)) {
42	    return (await Promise.all(
43	      files.map((file) => normalizeFile(file)),
44	    )) as RetType;
45	  }
46	  return (await normalizeFile(files)) as RetType;
47	};
48	
49	export const fileSave = (
50	  blob: Blob | Promise<Blob>,
51	  opts: {
52	    /** supply without the extension */
53	    name: string;
54	    /** file extension */
55	    extension: FILE_EXTENSION;
56	    mimeTypes?: string[];
57	    description: string;
58	    /** existing FileSystemFileHandle */
59	    fileHandle?: FileSystemFileHandle | null;
60	  },
61	) => {
62	  return _fileSave(
63	    blob,
64	    {
65	      fileName: `${opts.name}.${opts.extension}`,
66	      description: opts.description,
67	      extensions: [`.${opts.extension}`],
68	      mimeTypes: opts.mimeTypes,
69	    },
70	    opts.fileHandle,
71	    false,
72	  );
```

```typescript
import { APP_NAME } from "@excalidraw/common";

const DEFAULT_TITLE = "Excalidraw Whiteboard";

// characters not allowed in file names on common filesystems (Windows in
// particular), plus characters that are awkward to carry around in a URL
const INVALID_FILENAME_CHARS = /[<>:"/\\|?#%*\x00-\x1f]/g;

/** query param used to reflect the current file's name in the URL */
const TITLE_URL_PARAM = "title";

/**
 * Restricts a (user-supplied) file name down to characters that are safe to
 * use both as an actual file name and as a URL query param, so it can be
 * reflected in the address bar without needing to be percent-encoded into
 * illegibility.
 */
export const sanitizeFilenameForURL = (name: string): string => {
  return name.replace(INVALID_FILENAME_CHARS, "").trim().slice(0, 100);
};

/**
 * Reflects the currently open file's name (if any) in the document title and
 * in the URL, so the user can tell at a glance which file they're working on.
 * Intentionally only called once a file has actually been saved to disk or
 * opened from disk (i.e. `name` is non-null) — a scene that was never saved
 * keeps the generic app title and a clean URL.
 */
export const updateDocumentTitleAndURL = (name: string | null) => {
  const sanitizedName = name ? sanitizeFilenameForURL(name) : "";

  document.title = sanitizedName
    ? `${sanitizedName} - ${APP_NAME}`
    : DEFAULT_TITLE;

  const url = new URL(window.location.href);
  if (sanitizedName) {
    url.searchParams.set(TITLE_URL_PARAM, sanitizedName);
  } else {
    url.searchParams.delete(TITLE_URL_PARAM);
  }

  if (url.toString() !== window.location.href) {
    window.history.replaceState({}, document.title, url);
  }
};
```

All tests pass, no unexpected file changes remaining. Here's a summary:

**Branch**: created `feat/issue-file-name-in-title-url` off `master` (your working tree was on the unrelated `feat/issue-4-triangle-stamp-v2` branch, so I moved the changes over to avoid mixing it into that PR).

**What changed**:
1. [packages/excalidraw/data/blob.ts](packages/excalidraw/data/blob.ts) — when a `.excalidraw` file is opened (`loadSceneOrLibraryFromBlob`), the app now derives `appState.name` from the actual opened file's name (native file handle or the browser's `File.name`), stripped of its extension. Previously this was always lost, since `appState.name` isn't preserved in the exported JSON.
2. [excalidraw-app/data/fileTitle.ts](excalidraw-app/data/fileTitle.ts) — new small utility: `sanitizeFilenameForURL` strips characters invalid in file names/URLs, and `updateDocumentTitleAndURL` sets `document.title` to `"<name> - Excalidraw"` and reflects the sanitized name as a `?title=` query param, or resets both to the app default when there's no name.
3. [excalidraw-app/App.tsx](excalidraw-app/App.tsx) — wired that into the existing `onChange` handler (the same hot path used for autosaving), triggering only when `appState.name` actually changes, so it doesn't fire on every keystroke/edit.

**Why this satisfies the issue**: `appState.name` stays `null` for an untouched/untitled scene, so the title/URL stay generic. It only becomes non-null when the user opens an existing file (now, via the on-disk name) or explicitly saves/renames the project — matching "only show after the user has actually saved the item as a file." Filename sanitization happens right before it touches the URL.

Verified with `yarn test:typecheck`, `yarn fix` (lint clean), and `yarn test:update` (1502 tests passing). Changes are uncommitted — let me know if you'd like me to commit them.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-17 04:41:36Z)**_

All 1502 tests still pass. Fixed it: previously `actionSaveFileToDisk`/`actionSaveToActiveFile` only stored the returned `fileHandle` after a save, never touching `appState.name` — so the title/URL sync had nothing to react to. Now both actions set `appState.name` from the saved file's actual name (preferring the file handle's name, since the native Save dialog lets you pick a different filename than the one suggested), which flows through the existing `onChange` hook to update the title and URL.

---

```typescript
import { MIME_TYPES } from "@excalidraw/common";

import { loadFromBlob } from "./blob";

const validExcalidrawData = (appState: Record<string, unknown> = {}) =>
  JSON.stringify({
    type: "excalidraw",
    version: 2,
    source: "https://excalidraw.com",
    elements: [],
    appState,
    files: {},
  });

describe("loadFromBlob", () => {
  it("derives appState.name from the opened file's name (stripped of extension)", async () => {
    const file = new File([validExcalidrawData()], "My Diagram.excalidraw", {
      type: MIME_TYPES.excalidraw,
    });

    const { appState } = await loadFromBlob(file, null, null);

    expect(appState.name).toBe("My Diagram");
  });

  it("strips only the last extension when the file name contains dots", async () => {
    const file = new File(
      [validExcalidrawData()],
      "2024.roadmap.v2.excalidraw",
      { type: MIME_TYPES.excalidraw },
    );

    const { appState } = await loadFromBlob(file, null, null);

    expect(appState.name).toBe("2024.roadmap.v2");
  });

  it("falls back to null when the blob carries no file name", async () => {
    const blob = new Blob([validExcalidrawData()], {
      type: MIME_TYPES.excalidraw,
    });

    const { appState } = await loadFromBlob(blob, null, null);

    expect(appState.name).toBeNull();
  });

  it("prefers an explicitly supplied FileSystemFileHandle's name over the blob's own name", async () => {
    const file = new File([validExcalidrawData()], "blob-name.excalidraw", {
      type: MIME_TYPES.excalidraw,
    });

    const { appState } = await loadFromBlob(file, null, null, {
      name: "handle-name.excalidraw",
    } as unknown as FileSystemFileHandle);

    expect(appState.name).toBe("handle-name");
  });
});
```

```typescript
    fileSave: vi.fn(async () => ({
      name: "Renamed Diagram.excalidraw",
    })),
  };
});

describe("save-to-disk actions", () => {
  beforeEach(async () => {
    await render(<Excalidraw />);
  });

  it("actionSaveFileToDisk updates appState.name to the name the file was actually saved as", async () => {
    act(() => {

    await waitFor(() => {

      h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionSaveToActiveFile);

      expect(h.state.name).toBe("Renamed Diagram");
    });
  });
});
```

```typescript
import {

  updateDocumentTitleAndURL,

describe("sanitizeFilenameForURL", () => {
  it("strips characters that are unsafe in file names / URLs", () => {
    expect(sanitizeFilenameForURL('my<>:"/\\|?#%*file')).toBe("myfile");
  });

  it("trims surrounding whitespace", () => {
    expect(sanitizeFilenameForURL("  My Diagram  ")).toBe("My Diagram");
  });

    expect(sanitizeFilenameForURL(longName).length).toBe(100);
  });
});

describe("updateDocumentTitleAndURL", () => {
  const originalTitle = document.title;

  afterEach(() => {
    document.title = originalTitle;
    window.history.replaceState({}, "", "/");
  });

  it("reflects the file name in the document title and the URL", () => {
    updateDocumentTitleAndURL("My Diagram");

    expect(document.title).toBe("My Diagram - Excalidraw");
    expect(new URL(window.location.href).searchParams.get("title")).toBe(
      "My Diagram",
    );
  });

  it("resets to the default title and clears the URL param when name is null", () => {
    updateDocumentTitleAndURL("My Diagram");
    updateDocumentTitleAndURL(null);

    expect(document.title).toBe("Excalidraw Whiteboard");
    expect(new URL(window.location.href).searchParams.has("title")).toBe(
      false,
    );
  });

  it("preserves other parts of the URL (e.g. hash) when updating", () => {
    window.history.replaceState({}, "", "/?id=abc#room=1,2");

    updateDocumentTitleAndURL("My Diagram");

    const url = new URL(window.location.href);
    expect(url.searchParams.get("id")).toBe("abc");
    expect(url.hash).toBe("#room=1,2");
    expect(url.searchParams.get("title")).toBe("My Diagram");
  });
});

```
